title: A new-to-nature nitrogenase with no homology to natural nitrogenases

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 12, New nitrogenases. Target: a nitrogenase with no sequence or structural homology to the natural family that converts N2 to ammonia at rates of a similar order of magnitude to natural enzymes. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Nonhomologous nitrogenases
page.definition: A protein converts nitrogen gas (N₂) into ammonia at rates of a similar order of magnitude to natural nitrogenases, the enzymes that perform biological nitrogen fixation. Its sequence and three-dimensional structure lack detectable homology, similarity indicating common ancestry, to known nitrogenases and nitrogenase-like proteins.

goal.need: The energy consumption and direct CO₂ emissions of ammonia production, quantified below for 2020, motivate alternative synthesis routes. ANR's NITRO GENESE programme pursues bioinspired nitrogen fixation. FutureHouse and Edison Scientific pose the narrower scientific goal of reproducing nitrogenase activity outside the natural protein family; their challenge sets no industrial energy or emissions target.

statements.quote: Drawing inspiration from the Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, Edison Scientific and FutureHouse have assembled a set of Millennium Problems for Biology.
statements.context: The announcement, published on 23 September 2026, lists New nitrogenases as problem 12.

statements.quote: Nitrogen-fixing technologies inspired by biology are required to produce the ammonia needed for today’s society in a green, carbon-neutral manner.
statements.context: The coordinator's summary for the ANR–FNS 2024 call states a broader goal of bioinspired ammonia catalysis.

completion.title: A nonhomologous nitrogenase reaches the order of magnitude of natural nitrogenase reaction rates.
completion.criterion: A protein converts N₂ to ammonia at rates at least of a similar order of magnitude to naturally occurring nitrogenases, while falling well below sequence- and structure-similarity thresholds against all known nitrogenase and nitrogenase-like proteins. Discovery in nature, de novo design and engineering are permitted. The published acceptance conditions specify no numerical rate ratio, reference enzyme, assay conditions, similarity metric or similarity cutoff.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, published challenge acceptance conditions for problem 12, New nitrogenases, in The Millennium Problems for Biology.
completion.threshold_quote: Create a new nitrogenase that does not bear sequence or structural homology to the natural family.
completion.basis: These are the challenge setters' acceptance conditions. They require both catalytic performance and exclusion of the existing protein family. Their numerical boundaries remain unspecified, so the source does not yet provide a reproducible numerical pass/fail test. A reported ammonia yield alone cannot establish that the rate requirement has been met.

milestones.title: An engineered protein–cofactor complex reduces acetylene to ethylene.
milestones.criterion: The protein–cofactor complex produces ethylene from acetylene, measured by gas chromatography and compared with free-cofactor controls. This surrogate reaction establishes substrate-reduction activity without establishing N₂ reduction. The patent published on 26 March 2026 reports 11 purified designs from 38 constructs; ArtN2ase-10 retained 74% acetylene-reduction activity after 3 hours. These patent results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Nitrogen-fixation community; the acetylene-reduction convention is documented by Montes-Luz and colleagues for plants and bacteria and applied to artificial proteins in the cited patent.
milestones.threshold_quote: uses gas chromatography to measure the reduction of acetylene to ethylene by nitrogenase

milestones.title: An engineered protein converts isotope-labelled nitrogen gas into isotope-labelled ammonia.
milestones.criterion: Supplied ¹⁵N₂ becomes ¹⁵NH₃, detected as ¹⁵NH₄⁺, above contamination and protein-free controls. Patent Example 4 reports a turnover number of 11 ± 2 for cofactor-loaded ArtN2ase-10; the quantum-dot system alone and protein without cofactor produced no observable labelled ammonium. This is cumulative product per catalyst, not a reaction rate. The result is not peer reviewed; the cited paragraph does not state the replicate count or meaning of ±2.
milestones.set_by: Nitrogen-fixation community; isotope tracing is demonstrated by Schnabel and Sattely in biological nitrogen fixation and applied to artificial proteins in patent Example 4.
milestones.threshold_quote: from which we conclude that ammonia in the medium is de novo fixed from gaseous dinitrogen

milestones.title: A protein without nitrogenase sequence or structural homology catalyzes N₂ reduction to ammonia.
milestones.criterion: The same protein demonstrates N₂-to-ammonia catalysis and lacks detectable sequence and structural homology to all known nitrogenase and nitrogenase-like proteins. The natural-enzyme rate requirement remains for completion. The challenge supplies no numerical similarity cutoffs. The patent describes unrelated starting scaffolds but does not establish this exhaustive sequence-and-structure exclusion.
milestones.set_by: Atlas intermediate condition derived from problem 12; no separate outside acceptance test for this precompletion result was found in the challenge, programme descriptions or artificial-nitrogenase disclosures.

not_found: Problem 12 provides no numerical rate ratio, reference enzyme, assay conditions or sequence and structure similarity cutoffs.
No outside document located defines a separate precompletion test combining nitrogen reduction with exclusion of nitrogenase homology.
No peer-reviewed paper or independent replication of the reported ArtN2ase-10 nitrogen-reduction result was located.
The cited patent paragraph does not state the replicate count or meaning of ±2 for its turnover number.
